scenario: LSER.17.2: an infinite bracketing neighbour reads its limit -- the answer is x_lo when the pair is equal, or when x_lo is -inf under anything but +inf -- so only a [-inf, +inf] pair reaches the formula's NaN. Drives `s.p50` over a `ttl` schema (every assert absorbs, LSER.7.6.3, so two equal infinities are two samples) into the ring-buffer percentile of both runtimes. Three rows, one per `dev`, each two samples and a third assert whose pre-sample read (LSER.8.6.1) sees the pair: a = [inf, inf] reads inf (the formula alone: inf - inf is NaN); b = [-inf, 5] reads -inf (the formula alone: -inf + inf is NaN); c = [5, inf] reads inf (the formula agrees; the control). The one-sample reads before each pair read that sample. THE `where` READS A SERIES, SO IT IS RE-READ EVERY PUMP ([LTIM.2.4.1]) and each live fact fires once, on the pump its condition first holds ([LTIM.2.5.1]): each row's first fact, cold when it arrived, reads the one-sample value with the second, so each row's first message logs twice.
rules_ds:
use default

schema Sample scope ttl 1_d:
    dev: String
    level: Float

series Sample.level (by: dev):
    p50 sliding 1_h

rule r:
    Sample s where s.p50 is not null
->
    log info "{s.dev} {s.p50}"
